hypothesis: The canonical MorphologyCompiler can consume active generated native-meta OrganSpec implementation refs during every compile, emit typed reconstructible policy bindings, and fail closed on wrong/malformed/inconsistent refs while preserving legacy event-order behavior for genomes without native-meta refs.
falsifier: FAIL if canonical MorphologyCompiler.compile bypasses native-meta validation, if FULL descendant refs do not appear as typed compiled bindings, if REMOVE/bootstrap produces bindings, if WRONG kind or malformed refs compile, if SHUFFLE residual identity is accepted when an expected residual is frozen, if ordinary morphology compile output regresses, or if cold restart changes binding fingerprints.
full_control: Compile a cycle-1-style L3 descendant through canonical MorphologyCompiler and require a typed native-meta binding in the compiled runtime.
remove_control: Compile the identical parent morphology with bootstrap generator/mutator refs and require zero native-meta bindings.
wrong_control: Place a valid generator native-meta ref in a MUTATOR OrganSpec and require canonical compiler failure.
shuffle_control: Compile a valid ref generated for residual B under frozen expected residual A and require failure.
legacy_regression_control: MorphologyCompiler.compile returns the same event-order contract on legacy/no-policy genomes.
restart_control: Cold canonical compilation of the same descendant produces identical compiled-runtime fingerprint and policy-binding fingerprint.
